definition: Likely to cause strong disagreement or heated argument.
example: The referee's last-second call proved contentious, and fans debated it for weeks.
nuance: Contentious suggests heated, ongoing argument, while controversial can simply mean opinions are divided; it can also describe a quarrelsome person.
prompt: A book club must decide which novel to read next month.
options: Choosing the next novel proved contentious, and members argued for over an hour.
Everyone agreed on the first title at once, so the decision was quite contentious.
The contentious member read every assigned chapter on time and took careful notes.
After the pleasant meeting, she felt contentious and relaxed happily on the sofa.
reasons: A long, heated debate over the choice is exactly what makes a decision contentious.
Instant agreement is the opposite of a decision that sparks dispute.
This confuses the word with conscientious, which means diligent and careful.
This confuses the word with contented; relaxed satisfaction has nothing to do with quarreling.

practice.prompt: Two neighbors share an old wooden fence that needs repair.
options: Both neighbors gladly split the cost, so the matter was contentious from the very start.
The neighbor was so contentious that he measured every board twice before nailing it.
Who should pay for the new fence became a contentious question between the neighbors.
The contentious repair took only an hour because the boards were already cut to size.
reasons: Happy cooperation reverses the meaning; nothing here was fought over.
Careful, thorough work describes a conscientious person, not a quarrelsome one.
A cost both sides argue over is a matter that provokes dispute.
How quickly a job goes says nothing about whether it causes argument.
